note: Commemoration dates follow the app’s fixed-calendar data. Approximate dates are marked c.; uncertain details are stated cautiously.

martyrs.name: Martyr Basil of Ancyra
martyrs.about: A lay Christian who endured torture and confessed Christ during the persecution of Emperor Julian.
martyrs.commemoration: Circumcision of Our Lord; Saint Basil the Great

martyrs.name: Hieromartyr Theogenes of Parium
martyrs.about: A bishop who refused military service and pagan sacrifice, remaining steadfast through imprisonment and death.
martyrs.commemoration: Saint Seraphim of Sarov; Saint Sylvester of Rome

martyrs.name: New Martyr George of Iberia
martyrs.about: A Georgian Christian remembered for refusing conversion to Islam and accepting death rather than renouncing Christ.
martyrs.commemoration: Saint Seraphim of Sarov; Saint Sylvester of Rome

martyrs.name: Martyr Gordius
martyrs.about: A Roman soldier who left military service, returned publicly to confess Christ, and was executed.

martyrs.name: Hieromartyrs Theopemptus and Theonas
martyrs.about: A bishop and a former pagan magician who confessed Christ together during Diocletian’s persecution.
martyrs.commemoration: Eve of Theophany; Martyrs Theopemptus and Theonas

martyrs.name: Martyr Athanasius of Attalia
martyrs.about: A Christian of Attalia remembered for refusing apostasy and accepting execution under Ottoman rule.
martyrs.commemoration: Synaxis of Saint John the Baptist

martyrs.name: Martyr Tatiana
martyrs.about: A Roman deaconess who endured torture under Emperor Alexander Severus and remained faithful to Christ.

martyrs.name: Venerable Martyr Anastasius the Persian
martyrs.about: A former Persian soldier and monk who was tortured and killed after openly confessing Christianity.
martyrs.commemoration: Apostle Timothy; Venerable Martyr Anastasius the Persian

martyrs.name: Martyr Tryphon
martyrs.about: A young healer and confessor who suffered under Emperor Decius after refusing to sacrifice to idols.
martyrs.commemoration: Forefeast of the Meeting; Martyr Tryphon

martyrs.name: Hieromartyr Charalambos
martyrs.about: An aged bishop who preached Christ openly and endured severe torture during the reign of Septimius Severus.

martyrs.name: Great Martyr Theodore the Recruit
martyrs.about: A newly enlisted soldier who refused pagan sacrifice and was burned after boldly confessing Christ.

martyrs.name: Martyr Eudocia
martyrs.about: A convert who embraced prayer and charity, then suffered execution during the persecution under Trajan.

martyrs.name: Forty Martyrs of Sebaste
martyrs.about: Forty Christian soldiers exposed on a frozen lake after refusing to renounce Christ or offer pagan sacrifice.

martyrs.name: New Martyrs and Confessors associated with the Russian Church
martyrs.about: Clergy and laity who suffered imprisonment, exile, and death under militant atheistic persecution.

martyrs.name: Great Martyr George
martyrs.about: A Cappadocian soldier who confessed Christ before imperial authorities and was executed under Diocletian.

martyrs.name: Martyr Nike
martyrs.about: Remembered in Orthodox synaxaria as an early Christian witness; surviving biographical details are limited.

martyrs.name: Great Martyr Irene
martyrs.about: A royal-born convert who preached Christ and endured repeated torments while refusing idolatry.

martyrs.name: Hieromartyr Mocius
martyrs.about: A priest who disrupted a pagan sacrifice, confessed Christ, and was beheaded after prolonged torture.
martyrs.commemoration: Hieromartyr Mocius; Saints Cyril and Methodius

martyrs.name: Martyrs traditionally associated with the apostolic witness at Rome
martyrs.about: Christians remembered with the apostolic witness at Rome, where persecution claimed many early believers.

martyrs.name: Martyrs Cosmas and Damian
martyrs.about: Physician brothers who healed without payment and were killed after refusing to abandon their Christian faith.
martyrs.commemoration: Holy Unmercenaries Cosmas and Damian of Rome

martyrs.name: Great Martyr Euphemia
martyrs.about: A young Christian who endured torture under Diocletian and became closely linked with Chalcedon’s memory.

martyrs.name: Martyr Justus
martyrs.about: An early Christian martyr remembered for steadfast confession; surviving details vary among local calendars.
martyrs.commemoration: Apostle Aquila; Saint Nikodemos of the Holy Mountain

martyrs.name: Martyrs Cyricus and Julitta
martyrs.about: A mother and her young son who were killed during Diocletian’s persecution after refusing apostasy.

martyrs.name: Great Martyr Marina
martyrs.about: A young Christian who rejected idolatry and endured torture and execution during Diocletian’s reign.

martyrs.name: Great Martyr Christina
martyrs.about: A young convert who destroyed idols, endured family opposition and torture, and remained faithful unto death.

martyrs.name: Great Martyr Panteleimon
martyrs.about: A physician who treated the poor freely and was executed after confessing Christ before imperial authorities.

martyrs.name: Seven Maccabee Martyrs
martyrs.about: Seven brothers and their mother endured torture rather than violate God’s law under Antiochus IV.
martyrs.commemoration: Procession of the Holy Cross; Seven Maccabee Martyrs

martyrs.name: Martyr Anthony of Alexandria
martyrs.about: An Alexandrian Christian remembered in the synaxaria for faithful witness; historical details are sparse.

martyrs.name: Martyr Diomedes
martyrs.about: A Christian physician who healed without payment and was killed during the persecution under Diocletian.

martyrs.name: Saint John the Baptist
martyrs.about: The Forerunner was beheaded after condemning Herod’s unlawful marriage and bearing witness to moral truth.
martyrs.commemoration: Beheading of Saint John the Baptist

martyrs.name: Hieromartyr Cyprian of Carthage
martyrs.about: Bishop and theologian beheaded during Valerian’s persecution after refusing pagan sacrifice.
martyrs.commemoration: Placing of the Sash of the Theotokos

martyrs.name: Forty Women Martyrs and their teacher Ammon
martyrs.about: Christian women and their teacher who were tortured and killed for refusing pagan worship under Licinius.
martyrs.commemoration: Beginning of the Church Year; Saint Symeon the Stylite

martyrs.name: Martyr Severian
martyrs.about: A Christian senator who aided imprisoned believers and was tortured to death under Governor Lysias.

martyrs.name: Great Martyr Euphemia
martyrs.about: Her principal feast recalls her steadfast confession and martyrdom during the persecution of Diocletian.

martyrs.name: Sophia, Faith, Hope, and Love
martyrs.about: Three young sisters were martyred before their mother Sophia, who died after grieving at their tombs.
martyrs.commemoration: Martyrs Sophia, Faith, Hope, and Love

martyrs.name: Great Martyr Eustathius and his family
martyrs.about: A Roman commander, his wife, and sons were executed after refusing to sacrifice to pagan gods.
martyrs.commemoration: Great Martyr Eustathius and his family

martyrs.name: Protomartyr Thecla
martyrs.about: A disciple of Paul remembered for preaching, ascetic courage, and surviving repeated attempts to kill her.

martyrs.name: Martyrs Mardonius and Stratonikos
martyrs.about: Early Christian martyrs remembered for steadfast confession during imperial persecution.

martyrs.name: Cyprian and Justina
martyrs.about: A former magician and a Christian virgin who resisted spiritual coercion and were executed under Diocletian.
martyrs.commemoration: Hieromartyr Cyprian and Virgin Martyr Justina

martyrs.name: Martyrs Rusticus and Eleutherius
martyrs.about: Companions of Ignatius of Antioch who shared his journey and were martyred for confessing Christ.

martyrs.name: Martyr Eroteis
martyrs.about: An early Christian witness preserved in the synaxaria; reliable biographical information is limited.

martyrs.name: Sergius and Bacchus
martyrs.about: Roman officers stripped of rank and killed after their Christian faith was exposed under Maximian.

martyrs.name: Virgin Martyr Pelagia
martyrs.about: A young Christian who chose death rather than surrender her faith and chastity during persecution.

martyrs.name: Nazarius, Gervasius, Protasius, and Celsus
martyrs.about: Martyrs linked by the Milanese tradition and honored for missionary witness and steadfast confession.
martyrs.commemoration: Martyrs Nazarius, Gervasius, Protasius, and Celsus

martyrs.name: Martyr Marinus
martyrs.about: An early martyr commemorated for refusing apostasy; surviving accounts provide few secure details.

martyrs.name: Great Martyr Artemius
martyrs.about: A military governor who opposed Julian’s anti-Christian policies and was tortured and beheaded.

martyrs.name: Arethas and companions
martyrs.about: Arethas and many Christians of Najran were killed after refusing to renounce Christ.

martyrs.name: Great Martyr Demetrius
martyrs.about: A military saint and teacher imprisoned and killed for Christian witness during Diocletian’s persecution.

martyrs.name: Martyr Nestor
martyrs.about: A young Christian who faced the gladiator Lyaeus with Demetrius’s blessing and was later beheaded.

martyrs.name: Terence and Neonilla
martyrs.about: A married couple and their children who endured torture and death together during Christian persecution.
martyrs.commemoration: Protection of the Theotokos in Greek tradition; Martyrs Terence and Neonilla

martyrs.name: Cosmas and Damian
martyrs.about: Unmercenary physician saints remembered for healing freely; this pair is not always described as martyred.

martyrs.name: Onesiphorus and Porphyrius
martyrs.about: Christian companions tortured and killed during the persecutions of Diocletian and Maximian.

martyrs.name: Menas
martyrs.about: An Egyptian soldier who left the army, confessed Christ publicly, and was executed under Diocletian.
martyrs.commemoration: Great Martyr Menas; Martyrs Victor and Vincent

martyrs.name: Victor
martyrs.about: A Christian soldier tortured and killed after refusing pagan worship during the reign of Marcus Aurelius.
martyrs.commemoration: Great Martyr Menas; Martyrs Victor and Vincent

martyrs.name: Vincent
martyrs.about: A Spanish deacon who endured severe torture and died during Diocletian’s persecution.
martyrs.commemoration: Great Martyr Menas; Martyrs Victor and Vincent

martyrs.name: Martyr Antoninus
martyrs.about: An early Christian martyr whose name is preserved in the calendar though detailed records are limited.

martyrs.name: Great Martyr Catherine
martyrs.about: A learned Christian who challenged pagan arguments and was executed after refusing imperial coercion.

martyrs.name: Hieromartyr Peter of Alexandria
martyrs.about: Bishop of Alexandria beheaded during the final phase of Diocletian’s persecution.
martyrs.commemoration: Saint Clement of Rome; Hieromartyr Peter of Alexandria

martyrs.name: Great Martyr Barbara
martyrs.about: A young Christian killed after resisting family pressure and refusing to renounce her faith.
martyrs.commemoration: Great Martyr Barbara; Saint John of Damascus

martyrs.name: Martyr Diogenes
martyrs.about: An early Christian witness commemorated in the synaxaria; dependable biographical details are scarce.

martyrs.name: Martyr Niser
martyrs.about: A martyr preserved in local Orthodox memory; surviving historical information is limited.

martyrs.name: Martyr Synesius
martyrs.about: A Christian reader who was tortured and beheaded during the persecution of Emperor Aurelian.

martyrs.name: Five Martyrs of Sebaste
martyrs.about: Eustratius, Auxentius, Eugenius, Mardarius, and Orestes suffered together under imperial persecution.
martyrs.commemoration: Martyrs Eustratius, Auxentius, Eugenius, Mardarius, and Orestes

martyrs.name: Martyr Iacchus
martyrs.about: An early Christian martyr remembered by name in the calendar; further details are uncertain.
martyrs.commemoration: Prophet Daniel and the Three Holy Youths

martyrs.name: Hieromartyr Ignatius
martyrs.about: Bishop of Antioch who wrote pastoral letters en route to Rome, where he was killed in the arena.

martyrs.name: Venerable Martyr Eugenia
martyrs.about: An ascetic Christian who served others in disguise and was later executed during imperial persecution.
martyrs.commemoration: Eve of the Nativity; Venerable Martyr Eugenia

martyrs.name: Martyr Euthymius
martyrs.about: A Christian martyr commemorated after the Nativity; reliable details of his life remain limited.
martyrs.commemoration: Synaxis of the Most Holy Theotokos

martyrs.name: Protomartyr Stephen
martyrs.about: One of the first seven deacons, stoned after proclaiming Christ and forgiving those who killed him.

martyrs.name: Holy Innocents
martyrs.about: Children killed by Herod in the Gospel account, honored as innocent witnesses associated with Christ.

martyrs.name: Martyr Busiris
martyrs.about: An early Christian martyr preserved in the synaxaria; detailed historical evidence is limited.
